info.title: Codebase intelligence for C#.
info.description: Codebase intelligence for C# — dead code, duplicate, and health checks.

x-inspectra.cliParsedDescription: With no command, roe runs dead-code, dupes, and health together — the same thing as `roe check`.

options.description: Also flag enum members and public settable auto-properties

options.name: --root
options.description: Additional entry-point roots (fully-qualified symbol names)

options.name: --library
options.description: Project names to always treat in library mode (public API is used), regardless of executables elsewhere in the workspace

options.name: --format
options.description:
Output format
[default: human]
[possible values: human, json]

options.name: --mode
options.description:
Matching mode [default: exact]
Possible values:
- exact:    Exact token match — only verbatim copy-pasted blocks match
- semantic: Identifiers and numeric literals are normalized to a shared placeholder, so renamed-but-structurally-identical blocks match too

options.name: --no-code
options.description: Hide the duplicated source code printed under each group (human format only)

options.name: --min-tokens
options.description: Minimum token-run length for a match to be reported [default: 50]

options.name: --min-lines
options.description: Minimum line span (of the shortest occurrence) for a match to be reported [default: 5]

options.name: --min-occurrences
options.description: Minimum number of occurrences for a match to be reported [default: 2]

options.name: --config

commands.name: health
commands.description: Flag complexity, size, and coupling issues

options.name: --format
options.description:
Output format
[default: human]
[possible values: human, json]

options.name: --max-complexity
options.description: Flag methods/properties above this cyclomatic complexity [default: 10]

options.name: --max-cognitive
options.description: Flag methods/properties above this cognitive complexity — like cyclomatic, but weighted by how deeply nested the code is [default: 15]

options.name: --max-method-lines
options.description: Flag methods/properties whose body spans more than this many lines [default: 40]

options.name: --max-parameters
options.description: Flag methods/operators/indexers declared with more than this many parameters [default: 5]

options.name: --max-file-lines
options.description: Flag files longer than this many lines [default: 750]

options.name: --max-type-members
options.description: Flag types with more than this many members [default: 20]

options.name: --exclude-tests
options.description: Skip declarations in test projects — long arrange/act/assert methods and multi-case fixtures are normal there

options.name: --sort
options.description:
Order findings by how far past their threshold they sit, or by file path
Possible values:
- severity: Worst first, by how many times over its threshold each finding sits
- path:     Grouped by file path, ascending — stable regardless of the metrics
[default: severity]

options.name: --limit
options.description:
Print at most this many findings; 0 prints all of them
[default: 0]

options.name: --hotspots
options.description: Also rank the files that are both complex and frequently changed, read from git history. Informational — never affects the exit code

options.name: --top
options.description:
How many hotspots to list
[default: 10]

options.name: --baseline
options.description: Report only findings that this baseline file doesn't already record, so CI can gate on new debt in a codebase that already has some

options.name: --write-baseline
options.description: Record every current finding to this path and exit 0, printing no report. Writing through `--baseline` would record a filtered picture of the codebase, so the two conflict
